observation.visible_scene: Top-down view of a stainless-steel stockpot with two side handles resting on a gray surface, with a dark curved burner ring visible beneath it. The pot holds a dark brown liquid. Floating on the surface near the center is a tan/yellowish foam or scum mass composed of two main lobes (each with a small dark hole) and a thin tail trailing toward the lower right. A pale wooden block with partial printed text sits at the upper-left edge of the frame. A translucent white steam/vapor haze hovers over the liquid surface.
visible_changes: The steam/vapor continuously billows, thins, and shifts its position across the surface from frame to frame, at times partially veiling the left side, the top, or the right side of the foam and liquid.

The floating tan foam mass stays present on the surface throughout the excerpt; its overall shape, lobes, dark holes, and tail remain largely persistent, with only subtle apparent drift/rotation relative to the pot rim.
The dark liquid surface shows slight movement and shimmering beneath the foam and steam, consistent with gentle convection, but no new foam forms or disappears within the crop.
The pot, handles, burner ring, and wooden block keep a fixed position in the frame, indicating the camera is essentially stationary (only minor jitter possible).
outside_clip_unknowns: What the floating tan material is made of and how it originally formed.
Whether the liquid is at a rolling boil or a simmer before/after this segment, and the heat setting used.
Any stirring, skimming, or other operator action outside the cropped window.
Whether the foam would eventually break apart, sink, or be removed.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the foam's slight apparent drift (surface convection vs. tiny camera motion) cannot be resolved from the frames.
Whether the steam density changes reflect real vapor production or only its movement relative to the lens.
Precise material identities of the liquid and foam are not determinable visually.
